thread:
sasha: thinking out loud — what if we add a 'cold-write' fastpath that offloads evicted tensors as compressed delta pages to local NVMe instead of staging to host RAM?
kevin: curious — benefits? write amplification vs read cost tradeoff?
maria: main win is reducing host RAM pressure and GC churn during large bursts. NVMe is slower but we can compress and append, avoids paging noise on host.
sasha: exactly. sketch: compress with lightweight codec (lz4/fastlz), write contiguous delta segments, keep a small index in host RAM with offsets + checkpoints. read path decompress on demand or prefetch into host staging when we see a replay.
devon: worried about tail-latency on cache-miss reads. Decompress + NVMe seek might kill real-time requests.
zara: could mitigate with prioritization + admission control: hot tenants get prefetch credits, or we serve degraded models from a smaller in-memory cache if read latency would exceed SLO.
kevin: admission control seems key. We should avoid big cold-write storms — if many tenants are evicting at once NVMe IOPS/queue depth will spike. How do we backpressure?
sasha: proposal: per-tenant token bucket for offload writes + global circuit breaker. Also a background compactor that coalesces small segments every N minutes to reduce read seeks.
maria: config example (pseudo-yaml):
```yaml
offload:
  enabled: true
  codec: lz4_fast
  tenant_write_budget: 5mb/s
  global_iops_limit: 5000
  compaction_interval_secs: 120
  prefetch_policy: heuristic
```
kevin: that helps. What about durability guarantees — NVMe writes might fail on power loss; do we need to replicate to remote cold store?
sasha: for now treat cold-write as ephemeral backing for residency, not durable long-term. If tenant requests strict durability they should use dedicated host staging or object-store offload path. We document that NVMe cold-write is best-effort and ephemeral across host reboots.
devon: operationally, add telemetry: per-tenant offload rate, NVMe latencies, compaction backlog. Maybe evict-bot can alert when compaction backlog > threshold.
evict-bot: alert rule suggestion: offload_compaction_backlog_seconds > 300 -> pager to eng-runtime oncall. :warning:
maria: one more thing — fragmentation. If we append segments frequently, reads will hit many small fragments. Compactor needs to be IO-aware: batch by tenant timestamps, merge small fragments below 64KB into 1MB chunks.
zara: and we should expose per-tenant knobs so platform teams can tune budgets for bursty customers. Also add a low-overhead path to fall back to host RAM when NVMe saturates.
kevin: action items: (1) prototype append-only cold-write lib with lz4 + index, (2) simulate multi-tenant offload load to measure compaction/seek overhead, (3) add telemetry dims + circuit-breaker metrics. I'll pick up (1).
sasha: thanks — I'll write a short RFC addendum with the tradeoffs and the config sketch. Try to keep the prototype minimal: write/read + compact + simple admission API.
maria: +1. If we can show <2% tail increase for 95th pct read latency under realistic load it's a win.
devon: ping me when prototype works, I'll run SLO sims and failure injections.
sasha: cool — will post RFC link here when ready. :rocket:
